policy: Promotion requires repeated independent-domain evidence, identical observable obligations, explicit parameterization of local differences, no implied scientific equivalence, net engineering benefit, and shared tests that introduce no semantics.

decisions.reason: The reusable envelope and provenance obligations already exist; descriptor, predicate and symbolic semantics remain feature-local.
Exact references and immutable publication are already composable without a declaration-specific global contract.
Opaque payload transport and stable rejection are covered; provider gates differ by feature.
Observed in one Master feature and not independently replicated with identical predicate status semantics.
Potentially reusable symbolic type shape, but optional symbols and unresolved populations are not yet uniform across domains.
Mechanical exact propagation is already covered; scientific meanings remain distinct.
Required and optional provider modes are materially different and need lifecycle evidence before sharing.
The common structural gate is a composition of existing contracts; blocker, dependency and cardinality rules remain local.
Unsupported and scientifically blocked execution use different authoritative errors and cannot be merged safely.
Role binding is expressible by existing contracts while cardinality and context stay feature-local.
Exact reservation propagation is already represented without implying equivalence among unresolved items.
This is a global schema and reversible-identity policy issue, not a domain contract; explicit mappings remain local.
Existing contracts cover the mechanical envelope; evidence coverage and statuses differ.
Templates, symbols, errors and unresolved mappings are feature-owned; a future AST contract requires independent-domain equivalence.
A documentary non-promotion index is promising but currently supported by only two local observations.
The shared construction boundary is already composable; feature-specific identities and negative semantics remain explicit.
A future unevaluated-expression profile may be useful, but no common executable algebra or field set is authorized.
Candidate composition and state-versus-evolution ambiguity are explicitly different scientific boundaries.
Absent proof, partial proof and hypothesis status are not yet a single cross-domain vocabulary.
An eight-entry ordered sequence and a single fixed Principles role have different cardinality and scientific classification obligations.
All mechanical envelope obligations are already available; local pair, catalogue, cycle, AST, claim and profile semantics remain separate.
A generic exact-population validation profile may be useful only if errors, contextual constraints and relation checks remain parameterized.
Context-local catalogue order and cycle-stage order are observably different and cannot share one normative contract.
Tuple, equation, catalogue, constraint, invariant, operator and relation shapes differ in cardinality and ordering.
Fixed source-ordered collections recur, but counts, keys, documentary roles and errors are not identical.
A combined contract would risk erasing feature-specific source conditions; reversible mappings remain explicit.
Existing contracts already cover non-interpretation and propagation; empty, exact and provider-required cases remain distinct.
AST node meanings and role cardinalities differ across dynamics, membership, invariant, property and space records.
A provider lifecycle may be shareable only after concrete providers establish compatible input, output, error and determinism contracts.
Automatic aliasing could collide or hide scientifically meaningful source identifiers; mappings stay explicit and reversible.
Existing envelope contracts cover the common structure while operation meaning and forbidden scope remain local.
A composable base guard may be useful, but feature-specific integration, diagnosis and endpoint prohibitions must remain independently testable.
Only the mechanical propagation shape is shared; scientific ambiguity remains feature-specific.
Diagnostic observation and contextual virtue relations have different scopes; cross-domain review is still required.
Existing contracts cover exact maps and provenance without equating the scientific artifact kinds.
Ordered symbolic packaging and blockers are expressible by current contracts; AST and metric obligations remain local.
The profile is a composition of existing contracts; category, object-order, dependency and empty-relation rules remain feature-specific.
The shared opaque boundary is already covered; aggregate and provisional-separation semantics remain local.
A future decision-blocker profile may be useful, but decision identities, cardinalities and additional boundaries differ materially.
The isomorphic validation graph is already composable; exact counts, order and historical boundaries remain local.
Unsupported execution and specifically blocked scientific decisions are not yet a common cross-domain error contract.
Participant populations, identity-fusion rules, endpoint restrictions and unresolved counts differ across Relations features and other domains.
